cells.tense: There's a first thing in your hands right now and you're handling it carefully.
cells.ask: Show one piece of it to somebody this week and take in what they notice, without changing anything yet.
cells.core:
There's a first thing that's yours, and you're holding it lightly — enough to keep it intact, not so hard that it stops being yours. You haven't rushed it into a shape yet, and you haven't shown it before it's ready.

This is the balance: you're starting to give form to something, and you're not asking it to be finished. When it slips, it slips on the other side — the grip tightens, or you tell someone what it is before it knows what it is. Getting back doesn't take softer hands or firmer ones.

It takes letting someone else's strength sit under the work for a while, and that costs you the privacy of it. Show one piece this week. Their attention isn't a verdict. It just holds the thing up while you keep going.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the first of it — started, but not shaped yet.
cells.verb: starting to give form to the first thing that's yours
cells.place: the ground where what you are becomes visible in what you make

cells.tense: You're already at the finished version in your head, and the work is somewhere behind you.
cells.ask: Pick one part and bring it all the way to done, in its small form, before you plan the next.
cells.core:
You can see what this becomes and you're already living out there — the finished shape, the reaction, what it adds up to. So the part in front of you keeps getting measured against a version that doesn't exist yet, and it loses that comparison. The bracing is costing you the making.

This is the balance: your direction is doing the work. You choose what to do next from what you can see, not from what you're afraid of. At the moment the picturing runs far ahead of the doing.

Bring one part all the way to done in its small form. Not the best version, not the whole. When it's finished and it's still smaller than what you pictured, that isn't the answer getting handed down. Stay with it and let the next piece come from what's actually in front of you.
cells.sheetLine: You're building the finished version and living in it.
cells.verb: starting to give form to the first thing that's yours
cells.place: the ground where what you are becomes visible in what you make

cells.tense: There's something that hasn't been given a shape, and it's been that way for a while now.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person what you're making, in plain words, today — no showing, no explaining.
cells.core:
The thing you make stays unmarked, and nobody's seen it — including you, most days. Asking what it is feels like it might come back worse than not asking. Starting got set down at some point, and you've been standing on the other side of that since.

This is the balance: what you are becomes visible in what you make, without you having to announce it. At the moment the making is quiet and the shape stays vague.

The current comes back by turning toward what's clear, not by pushing harder into the making. Say to one person what you're making, in plain words. Not a pitch, not a defence. Hearing yourself name it does the work, and the plainness of it is the point. You don't have to make anything of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're making it and not letting anyone know it exists.
cells.verb: starting to give form to the first thing that's yours
cells.place: the ground where what you are becomes visible in what you make

cells.tense: You're shaping what's around you and you're calling it the situation doing it.
cells.ask: Name one call you already made this week — out loud, to yourself — as yours, and leave it that way.
cells.core:
The form is taking shape, and you're in the middle of it — deciding what stays, what gets said, which way this tilts. You talk about it like you're reading a report of something happening elsewhere. The making is going on by itself; the part where it's yours has gone quiet.

This is the balance: what you are shows in what you make, and you don't have to announce it. It bends when your hand in it goes missing — when the thing shapes itself and you're the one standing nearby.

Go back to the simpler form: one call this week, said as yours, no explanation attached. You don't have to call it a calling or mean anything by it. Just stop handing it to the situation, and notice that you can.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping this and you say it's the situation shaping you.

cells.place: the ground where what you are becomes visible in what you make

attempts.check: The record doesn't say the person has anything begun and abandoned; Too Little must locate them at a stopped offering without naming what happened behind them. The reader could fairly say they've simply never started and nothing is behind them — the ask still works, because describing one thing to one other person is useful either way. The sentence that would serve the writer more than the person is any line making them out as sitting on a talent, so I've kept the radiance out of the draft entirely.
